deliverables: WP1 - Plutarch and Ply Maintenance, Compatibility & Developer Experience
Bug fixes, correctness improvements, and optimizations
Documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements
request.recipient: Intersect treasury reserve smart contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor MLabs.
request.what: Annual treasury funding for MLabs Core Tool Maintenance & Enhancement for Plutarch and Ply, including maintenance, compatibility, bug fixes, optimizations, documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements.

claims.claim: Plutarch is a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts via controlled compilation into UPLC, and Ply serializes Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types.
MLabs says Plutarch and Ply have been extensively used across the Cardano ecosystem and reports an internal audit count of at least 26 teams building with them.
The rationale separately says MLabs conservatively counted at least 15 teams building with Plutarch and Ply.
MLabs’ public cross-language benchmarks are cited as showing Plutarch scripts ranking among the smallest in the benchmark suite with comparatively low on-chain compute and memory.
The proposal states that if Plutarch and Ply fall behind ledger and Plutus/UPLC evolution, existing adopters may face more friction, migration risk, bespoke workarounds, or avoidable rewrites.

The proposal says it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposer states the requested amount did not at submission, alone or in aggregate, breach the 350M ada Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
The budget totals 1,162,746 ada, consisting of 1,128,880 ada for Plutarch and Ply maintenance, compatibility, and developer experience plus a 33,866 ada Intersect budget administration fee.

The document discloses prior MLabs funding for Plutarch/Ply and related tooling through Project Catalyst, Intersect, and listed governance actions, including Fund9 USD 73,040, Fund13 ADA 487,679, Fund13 ADA 57,370, and ADA 70,000 from Intersect for Conway-era Plutarch updates.

Intersect says funds will be administered through 2026 Treasury Reserve and Project-Specific Smart Contracts with specified addresses, oversight committee participants, multisignature-style authorization thresholds, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada for annual Plutarch and Ply maintenance and enhancement, submitted by Intersect on behalf of MLabs, with stated work focused on compatibility, vulnerabilities, bug fixes, optimization, documentation, and developer experience; the strongest documentary support is for budget structure, governance process references, on-chain administration details, and external benchmark/process links, while adoption counts and risk-of-nonfunding claims are mainly proposer assertions.
